title: Galois clopen component covers and geometric-fibre stabilizer orbits
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $e_0/e$ be a finite Galois extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-pc-field-tower] (finite-dimensional, separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and normal: every irreducible polynomial over $e$ with a root in $e_0$ splits over $e_0$), and let $B$ be a nonempty integral $e$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Put $Y=B\times_e\operatorname{Spec}e_0$ and let $p:Y\to B$ be its projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose that the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $Y$ form a finite disjoint covering by nonempty open and closed subschemes $X_i$, each with its induced open subscheme structure. Put $A=\operatorname{Aut}_e(e_0)$ and use its canonical left action $a\mapsto\operatorname{id}_B\times\operatorname{Spec}(a^{-1})$ on $Y$. For every geometric point $\bar b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$, where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], the geometric fibre $Y_{\bar b}=Y\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] (formed along $\bar b$) is a nonempty finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $A$ acts simply transitively on its geometric points, with their residue-field embeddings retained. The action of $A$ on the components $X_i$ is transitive. For each component $X_i$, put $H_i=\{a\in A:aX_i=X_i\}$, with its restricted action on $X_i$, and $u_i=p|_{X_i}$. Then $u_i$ is finite, etale and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-etale-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and every geometric fibre of $u_i$ is nonempty and is a single $H_i$-orbit. Equivalently, any two maps $x,y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X_i$ over the same geometric point of $B$ satisfy $y=h\circ x$ for some $h\in H_i$.

proof.text: Write $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}e_0\to\operatorname{Spec}e$. A finite $e$-basis of $e_0$ generates it as an $e$-module, so the finite-spectrum equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-ring-map-finite], now recorded as the Mathlib leaf AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.SpecMap_iff, makes $\pi$ finite. Separability gives etaleness by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]. Both field spectra have exactly one point by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so $\pi$ is surjective. The projection $p$ is its base change along $B\to\operatorname{Spec}e$; apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] to conclude that $p$ is finite, etale and surjective. These base-change results impose no finiteness assumption on $B$.

Fix $\bar b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$. Apply [lem-galois-geometric-fibre] to $p$ to obtain a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ over $\Omega$. Its set of components is nonempty, because [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] makes $Y_{\bar b}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ surjective. Each copy has a unique $\Omega$-section, so its underlying point and its $\Omega$-valued geometric lift agree. By the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], maps $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ with $p x=\bar b$ correspond to maps $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}e_0$ over $\operatorname{Spec}e$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], these correspond bijectively to $e$-embeddings $\tau:e_0\hookrightarrow\Omega$. We retain these actual embeddings, rather than just their prime-ideal kernels.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), with Tag 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective); geometric lifts are identified by the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: Under Step 2 the automorphism $\operatorname{id}_B\times\operatorname{Spec}(a^{-1})$ sends $\tau$ to $\tau\circ a^{-1}$, by contravariance of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the functoriality in [def-pc-fibre-product]. The identity acts identically, and applying $b$ then $a$ sends $\tau$ to $\tau\circ b^{-1}\circ a^{-1}=\tau\circ(ab)^{-1}$, proving the left-action law. Finite dimensionality makes $e_0/e$ algebraic, and normality is assumed, so [lem-sfb-normal-embeddings-automorphism-transitive] says any embedding $\rho$ has the form $\tau\circ\sigma$ for some $\sigma\in A$. Taking $a=\sigma^{-1}$ proves transitivity. If $\tau\circ a^{-1}=\tau\circ b^{-1}$, injectivity of $\tau$ gives $a^{-1}=b^{-1}$ and hence $a=b$. Thus the action is simply transitive on the full geometric fibre, including its residue-field embeddings.

source.place: Tag 0BR4 (lemma-normal-embeddings-differ-by-aut), together with the inverse convention for the left action.

proof.text: The integral scheme $B$ is irreducible by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Each $X_i$ is nonempty and clopen with its open subscheme structure, exactly the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-finite-etale-clopen-restriction] for $p$. Therefore $u_i$ is finite, etale and surjective. Its base change along any $\bar b$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], hence nonempty. Applying [lem-galois-geometric-fibre] to $u_i$ also shows that this fibre is a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$; in particular it has an $\Omega$-valued lift. No assumption that $B$ is normal, proper, Noetherian or of finite type was used.

source.place: Tags 035C (lemma-closed-immersion-finite), 01WK (lemma-composition-finite), 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale), 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), 03WT (lemma-etale-open), 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective), and 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field); apply the already stated clopen restriction result.

proof.text: Every $a\in A$ induces a homeomorphism of $Y$. A homeomorphism sends irreducible subsets to irreducible subsets, and applying its inverse shows that maximal such subsets remain maximal; thus it permutes the components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Choose $b\in B$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(b)$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; the residue-field description in [def-weil-geometric-point] gives a geometric point $\bar b$. For any $i,j$, Step 4 gives lifts $x$ into $X_i$ and $y$ into $X_j$ over this same $\bar b$. Step 3 gives $a\in A$ with $y=a\circ x$. Consequently $aX_i$ and $X_j$ share the image point of $y$. Distinct components are disjoint by hypothesis, so $aX_i=X_j$. This proves transitivity on components.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150: G transitively permutes the components of X_0; elementary component argument using the established fibre transitivity.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and $\bar b$, and let $x,y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X_i$ lie over $\bar b$. View them as lifts into $Y$. By Step 3 there is $a\in A$ carrying $x$ to $y$. The components $aX_i$ and $X_i$ share the image of $y$, so Step 5 and disjointness force $aX_i=X_i$, that is, $a\in H_i$. Restricting the automorphism to the invariant open subscheme $X_i$ gives $h\in H_i$ with $y=h\circ x$ as morphisms: equality into $Y$ implies equality into its open subscheme. The stabilizer is a subgroup since products and inverses preserve $X_i$. Each such automorphism is over $B$, so this is an action on every geometric fibre. Those fibres are nonempty by Step 4, and the displayed equality proves that each is a single $H_i$-orbit. Conversely a single orbit is precisely this equality for any two lifts.

lean.statement: theorem galois_clopen_component_cover (e L : Type u) [Field e] [Field L] [Algebra e L] [Module.Finite e L] [Algebra.IsSeparable e L] [Normal e L] (B : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral B] (b : B ⟶ Spec (.of e)) (Y : Scheme.{u}) (p : Y ⟶ B) (q : Y ⟶ Spec (.of L)) (hY : IsPullback p q b (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap e L)))) (I : Type v) [Finite I] (U : I → Y.Opens) (hcomp : ∀ i : I, (U i : Set Y) ∈ irreducibleComponents Y) (hclosed : ∀ i : I, IsClosed (U i : Set Y)) (hdisjoint : Pairwise (fun i j : I ↦ Disjoint (U i) (U j))) (hcover : iSup U = ⊤) : ∃ a : (L ≃ₐ[e] L) →* Aut Y, (∀ g : L ≃ₐ[e] L, (a g).hom ≫ p = p ∧ (a g).hom ≫ q = q ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom g.symm.toRingHom)) ∧ (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ B), (∃ (J : Type u) (_ : Finite J) (_ : Nonempty J), Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.snd p t) ≅ Over.mk (Sigma.desc fun _ : J ↦ 𝟙 (Spec (.of Ω))))) ∧ (∃ x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y, x ≫ p = t) ∧ ∀ (x y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y), x ≫ p = t → y ≫ p = t → ∃! g : L ≃ₐ[e] L, x ≫ (a g).hom = y) ∧ (∀ i j : I, ∃ g : L ≃ₐ[e] L, (a g).hom '' (U i : Set Y) = (U j : Set Y)) ∧ ∀ i : I, ∃ (H : Subgroup (L ≃ₐ[e] L)) (r : H →* Aut (U i).toScheme), (∀ g : L ≃ₐ[e] L, g ∈ H ↔ (a g).hom '' (U i : Set Y) = (U i : Set Y)) ∧ (∀ h : H, (r h).hom ≫ (U i).ι = (U i).ι ≫ (a h.val).hom) ∧ IsFinite ((U i).ι ≫ p) ∧ Etale ((U i).ι ≫ p) ∧ Surjective ((U i).ι ≫ p) ∧ ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ B), (∃ x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ (U i).toScheme, x ≫ (U i).ι ≫ p = t) ∧ ∀ (x y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ (U i).toScheme), x ≫ (U i).ι ≫ p = t → y ≫ (U i).ι ≫ p = t → ∃ h : H, x ≫ (r h).hom = y
